To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the bunches with parabolically shaped line charge profile are more stable against the space-charge induced beam instabilities than the bunches with rectangular shaped line charge profile and (b) the bunches can be stabilized against the space- charge induced beam instabilities by using the slow waves and the fast waves.

(a) the longitudinal phase velocity of the bunch is a function of its line charge profile and its length-to-rms-width ratio, (b) the bunch can support a slow wave, (c) the slow wave can propagate with the bunch and can be used to modulate its energy and charge, and (d) a fast wave can propagate in the bunch and its velocity is a function of the bunch length-to-rms width ratio.

1) The longitudinal dynamics of space charge dominated electron bunches are governed by the nonlinear Schrodinger equation (NSE), and 2) The NSE predicts a new type of instability, which is called the modulational instability.
